ema: Buy when EMA 20 crosses above EMA 50 (RSI < 70), sell short on the opposite cross. SL 1.5 ATR, TP 3 ATR.
breakout: Buy when price breaks the high of the last 20 hours, sell short below the low. 2.5 ATR trailing stop, exit at the opposite 10 h channel.
meanrev: Buy when price closes below the lower Bollinger band with RSI < 30, sell short above the upper band with RSI > 70. Exit back at the 20 h average. SL 1.5 ATR.
macd: Buy when the MACD crosses above its signal line and price is above the EMA 200, sell short in the opposite case. SL 2 ATR, TP 4 ATR.
supertrend: Buy when the Supertrend turns bullish, sell short when it turns bearish. The stop follows the Supertrend line.
sma1060: FOREX.com guide: buy when the 10 h average crosses above the 60 h average, sell short on the opposite cross. Always in a position: each cross closes and reverses. 3 ATR protective stop.
pvt: PVT guide: buy when the Price Volume Trend crosses above its 21 average (rising buying pressure) and price is above the EMA 50 (confirmation), sell short in the opposite case. SL 1.5 ATR, TP 3 ATR. Volume = PAXG on Coinbase.
fibo: UK Gold Trading Experts guide: in the direction of the daily trend (price vs MA200, MA20 vs MA50), wait for a 38.2–61.8% pullback of the last impulse (48 h) then a reversal candle (hammer / engulfing). Stop beyond 78.6%, 127.2% extension target, stop to break-even after +1R then trailing.
hold: Not a strategy: buys the market at start and holds it. Used for comparison — a strategy that does no better adds nothing.
tsmom: In-house, based on time-series momentum (Moskowitz et al., 2012): gold tends to keep going in the direction of its last 3 months. Buy when price is above its 200-day average AND up over 3 months; exit as soon as one condition fails. Never short (gold rises over the long run). 4 ATR protective stop.
tsmom_ls: In-house: like trend momentum, but also sells short when price is below its 200-day average AND down over 3 months.
turtle: In-house, based on the Turtles' system 2: buy a 55-period high, sell short a 55-period low, exit on the opposite 20 channel. 2 ATR stop.
rsi2: RSI 2 (pullback in the trend, long only)
In-house, after Larry Connors: in an uptrend (price > 200 average), buy a very short pullback (RSI 2 < 10) and sell as soon as price gets back above its 5 average. 3 ATR stop.
pullback: RSI pullback in the EMA 50/200 trend

In-house: trend set by EMA 50 vs EMA 200; buy when RSI 14 gets back above 40 after a pullback (sell short when it falls back below 60 in a downtrend). Exit at RSI > 70 / < 30 or on a trend change. 2 ATR stop.
keltner: In-house: buy when price closes more than 2 ATR above its EMA 20 (unusually strong move), sell short below. 3 ATR trailing stop, exit if price crosses back over the EMA 50.
asia: In-house: gold is calm during the Asian session (00–07 UTC) then moves at the London open. Buy on the first close above the Asian high (sell short below the low) between 07 and 12 UTC; stop on the other side of the range, target = 1 range, forced exit at 20:00 UTC.
ichimoku: Japanese classic: buy when price is above the cloud AND the tenkan is above the kijun, sell short in the opposite case. Exit when price crosses back over the kijun. 2.5 ATR stop.
adx: Classic (Wilder): only enters when the trend is strong (ADX > 25), in the direction of +DI / −DI. Exit when the DIs cross or ADX falls back below 20. 3 ATR trailing stop.
squeeze: In-house, after John Bollinger: when the bands are the tightest in 6 months (sleepy market), enter in the direction of the first close outside the bands. 2.5 ATR trailing stop, exit if price crosses back over the 20 average.
ribbon: In-house: buy when EMA 10, 20 and 50 line up in bullish order (10 > 20 > 50), sell short in bearish order. Exit when EMA 10 crosses back over EMA 20. 2 ATR stop.
insidebar: Price action: an inside candle (contained in the previous one) marks a pause; enter on the break of the mother candle, only in the trend direction (price vs 200 average and EMA 20 vs 50). Stop on the other side of the mother candle, target 2× the risk.
heikin: Classic: buy on a clean green Heikin-Ashi candle (no lower wick) above the EMA 50, sell short on a red one with no upper wick below the EMA 50. Exit at the first color change. 2 ATR stop.
vote: In-house: 5 trend indicators vote (price vs 200 average, 10 vs 60 average, EMA 20 vs 50, MACD vs signal, 3-month gain). Buy when at least 4 vote up, sell short when at least 4 vote down, exit when the vote turns neutral or opposite. 4 ATR stop. Diversifying signals usually makes it more robust.
dollar: In-house: gold often rises when the dollar falls. Buy when EUR/USD is above its 50-day average (weak dollar) AND gold is above its EMA 50; sell short when the dollar is strong AND gold is below its EMA 50. Exit as soon as one condition fails. 3 ATR stop.
s_emavwap: Classic scalp: EMA 9 / EMA 21 cross in the direction of price vs the session VWAP. Stop 1 ATR, target 1.5 ATR, everything closed at 20:00 UTC.
s_vwaprev: Counter-trend: when price moves more than 2 standard deviations from the session VWAP with an extreme RSI 7 (< 20 or > 80), bet on a return to VWAP. Stop 1 ATR, exit at VWAP.
s_bbrsi: Counter-trend: close outside the Bollinger bands (20, 2) with an extreme RSI 7 → back toward the 20 average. 1 ATR stop.
s_orb: Range of the first 30 minutes of London (07:00 UTC) and New York (13:30 UTC); entry on the first close outside the range within the next 2 h. Stop on the other side of the range, target 1.5× the risk. Exit at 12:00 (London) / 17:00 UTC (New York).
s_stoch: Pullback in the short trend: price above a rising EMA 50, buy when the stochastic (14, 3, 3) turns up from below 20; opposite in a downtrend. Stop 1 ATR, target 1.5 ATR.
s_burst: Momentum: 3 consecutive candles in the same direction, total move > 2 ATR and close near the extreme → follow the move. Stop 1 ATR, target 1 ATR.
tom: Calendar effect documented on stock indices (Ariel 1987, Lakonishok & Smidt 1988): savings flows arrive at the end / start of the month. Buy at the close of the second-to-last business day of the month, sell at the close of the 3rd trading day of the next month. 3 ATR stop.
ibs: IBS: close at the day's low

Well-known very short-term mean reversion on indices: when the index closes in the bottom 20% of its day (IBS < 0.2) above its 200-day average, buy; sell when it closes near the top of its day (IBS > 0.8) or above the previous day's high. 3 ATR stop.
double7: Larry Connors: above the 200-day average, buy when the index closes at its 7-day low, sell when it closes at its 7-day high. 3 ATR stop.
down3: In-house: in an uptrend (price > 200 average), buy after 3 lower closes in a row, sell at the first higher close. 3 ATR stop.
sma200: The best-known market timing rule (Faber 2007): stay invested while the index is above its 200-day average (with a 2% margin to avoid whipsaws), get out below it. Keeps most of the gains and avoids the core of crashes. 5 ATR protective stop.
vixspike: In-house: when the VIX (fear index) is 25% above its 20-day average while the index stays above its 200-day average, buy the panic; sell when the VIX falls back below its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
vixcalm: In-house: be invested when fear is low (VIX below its 50-day average) and the index is above its 50-day average; get out when the VIX is 10% above its 50-day average or the index falls below its 50 average. 4 ATR stop.
season: Often-cited seasonal effect: physical gold demand rises from August to February (wedding and festival season in India, Chinese New Year). Invested from August to end of February, out from March to July. 4 ATR protective stop.
yields: Gold pays no interest: it often rises when rates fall. Buy when the US 10-year yield is below its 50-day average (falling rates) AND gold is above its EMA 50; sell short in the opposite case. Exit as soon as one condition fails. 3 ATR stop.
dxy: Like "Dollar + gold", but with the real dollar index (DXY, 6 currencies): buy when the DXY is below its 50-day average AND gold is above its EMA 50; sell short in the opposite case. 3 ATR stop.
fear: Gold is a safe haven when markets are scared: buy when the VIX is 10% above its 50-day average AND gold is above its 50-day average; exit when the VIX falls back below its average or gold below its 50 average. 3 ATR stop.
mom12: Classic absolute momentum (Antonacci): invested while gold is up over the last 12 months, out otherwise. 5 ATR protective stop.
high52: In-house: buy when gold closes at its 52-week high (new highs attract buyers), sell at its 50-day low. 4 ATR trailing stop.
halloween: Halloween effect (Bouman & Jacobsen 2002), seen on most stock markets for decades: invested from November to end of April, out from May to October. 5 ATR protective stop.
cumrsi: Larry Connors: above the 200-day average, buy when the sum of the last two days' RSI 2 drops below 35; sell when RSI 2 goes above 65. 3 ATR stop.
pctb: Mean reversion: above the 200-day average, buy a close below the lower Bollinger band (%b < 0); sell back at the 20-day average. 3 ATR stop.
lowvol: Crashes come when volatility explodes: invested when 20-day volatility is below its one-year average AND the index is above its 200-day average; exit if volatility is 10% above its average or the index falls 2% below its 200 average. 5 ATR stop.
rates: Growth stocks (tech) benefit from falling rates: invested when the US 10-year yield is below its 50-day average AND the Nasdaq is above its 50-day average; exit as soon as one condition fails. 4 ATR stop.
dip5: In-house: above the 200-day average, buy when the index closes 5% below its 20-day high; sell when it gets back to its 20-day high. 3 ATR stop.
tuesday: Calendar effect known to traders: a down Monday is often followed by an up Tuesday. Buy at the close of a down Monday (above the 200-day average), sell at the next close. 2 ATR stop.
golden: The most followed trend signal: invested while the 50-day average is above the 200-day average ("golden cross"), out after the "death cross". 5 ATR protective stop.
trendmix: In-house, inspired by trend-following funds: check whether price is up over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months. Invested when at least 3 of 4 horizons are up, exit when only one or none is left. 5 ATR stop.
mom12_1: Academic momentum variant (Jegadeesh & Titman): the 12-month gain ignoring the last month, which is often misleading short term. Invested if positive, out otherwise. 5 ATR stop.
dualmom: Antonacci (Dual Momentum): each month, compare the 12-month gain of gold and the Nasdaq. Invested in this market only if it is up AND beats the other; the two accounts hand over to each other. 5 ATR stop.
season200: Combination of two retained strategies: invested from August to February (season) ONLY if gold is above its 200-day average. Less time in the market, fewer drawdowns. 4 ATR stop.
seasonplus: Invested from August to February (season), and also the rest of the year when gold is clearly above its 200-day average (+2%). Keeps the season and catches big spring rallies. 4 ATR stop.
silver: When silver rises faster than gold (the gold / silver ratio drops below its 50-day average), it often starts a rally in all metals. Buy gold if it is also above its 50 average; exit as soon as one condition fails. 3 ATR stop.
riskoff: Gold gets bought when stocks struggle: invested when the Nasdaq 100 is below its 50-day average AND gold is above its own; exit when the Nasdaq gets back above or gold breaks its average. 3 ATR stop.
macro: In-house: three lights — Nasdaq above its 200-day average, VIX below its 50-day average, US 10-year yield below its 50-day average. Invested when at least 2 of 3 lights are green, out when one or none is left. 5 ATR stop.
sox: Chips (SOX index) often lead the rest of tech: invested when the SOX AND the Nasdaq are above their 50-day average, exit as soon as one falls below. 4 ATR stop.
dollarweak: A falling dollar helps big tech companies (foreign revenue): invested when the dollar index (DXY) is below its 50-day average AND the Nasdaq is above its own; exit as soon as one condition fails. 4 ATR stop.
macd_long: Buy when the MACD crosses above its signal line and price is above the EMA 200. SL 2 ATR, TP 4 ATR. Long-only version: never sells short.
ema_long: Buy when EMA 20 crosses above EMA 50 (RSI < 70). SL 1.5 ATR, TP 3 ATR. Long-only version: never sells short.
x_trendpb: Scalp pullback to EMA 20 in the 1 h trend

Bullish 1 h trend (EMA 20 > EMA 50, price above): buy when a candle touches the EMA 20 then closes above it, up. Stop below the low of the last 5 candles, target 2× the risk. Opposite in a downtrend. Everything closed at the end of the session.
x_vwapbounce: Price has stayed above the session VWAP for at least 1 h, in a bullish 1 h trend; it comes back to touch the VWAP and bounces (close above, up) → buy. Stop 1 ATR below VWAP, target 2× the risk. Opposite on the downside.
x_rangesweep: Scalp stop hunt of the overnight range

Gold: Asian range (00–06 UTC); Nasdaq: pre-market range (04:00–09:30 New York). In the first 3 hours of the session, if price breaks one edge of the range then closes back inside (stops were hunted), trade the other way: stop beyond the wick, target the other edge of the range.
x_pdsweep: Scalp false break above / below the previous day
Price breaks the previous day's high (or low) then closes back below (above) with a reversal candle → trade back toward VWAP. Stop beyond the wick, target VWAP (at least 1.2× the risk).
x_orb5: Range of the session's first 5-min candle (09:30 New York; 07:00 UTC for gold). Breakout in the 1 h trend direction, with volume above 1.5× average, within 90 minutes: stop on the other side of the range, target 2× the risk.
x_lasthalf: Effect documented on US indices (Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, 2018): the day's direction up to 15:30 New York (since the previous close) tends to continue into the last half hour. Buy (or sell) at 15:30, exit at 15:55. 1.5 ATR stop. For gold: same idea at the end of the New York session (19:30 → 19:55 UTC).
x_rsi2: Scalp RSI 2 in the 1 h trend
Short mean reversion: bullish 1 h trend and RSI 2 below 5 (several down candles in a row) → buy; exit when RSI 2 gets back above 60. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite in a downtrend (RSI 2 > 95).
x_squeeze: The Bollinger bands (20, 2) are the tightest of the last 100 candles (compressed market); on the first close outside the bands in the 1 h trend direction, enter. Stop at the 20 average, target 2× the risk.
x_break20: In the 1 h trend, a close above the high of the previous 20 candles with volume above 1.5× average → buy. Stop below the low of the last 5 candles, target 2× the risk. Opposite on the downside.
f_pullback: FTMO: 1 h pullback in the daily trend

Bullish daily trend (daily EMA 20 > EMA 50, price above): on 1 h candles, buy when price touches the EMA 20 and closes above it, up, above the EMA 50. Stop below the low of the last 6 hours, target 2× the risk, everything closed before the end of the session. Opposite in a downtrend.
f_pdbreak: Bullish daily trend: buy on the first 1 h close above the previous day's high during the session. Stop below the low of the last 4 hours, target 2× the risk, closed before the end of the session. Opposite below the previous day's low in a downtrend.
f_nightbreak: FTMO: overnight range breakout in the trend

Overnight range (gold: 00–07 UTC, before London; Nasdaq: 04:00–09:30 New York, before the open). In the first 3 hours of the session, a 1 h close outside the range in the daily trend direction: stop on the other side of the middle of the range, target 2× the risk.
f_insideday: After an inside day (high and low inside the previous day: the market is compressing), a daily close above the previous day's high in an uptrend (price > 50-day average) → buy. Stop below the inside day's low, target 2× the risk. Opposite on the downside.
f_nr7: FTMO: breakout after the calmest day (NR7)

Toby Crabel: the day with the narrowest high-low range of the last 7 (NR7) often comes before a move. Next close above its high, in the trend (price > 50-day average) → buy; stop below its low, target 2× the risk. Opposite on the downside.
f_weekbreak: Daily close above the previous week's high, price above the 50-day average → buy. 2 ATR stop, then a trailing stop 3 ATR below the highest high. Opposite below the previous week's low.
m_ibs: Close at the candle's low, in the trend

Higher-timeframe uptrend; the candle closes in the bottom 15% of its range and below the EMA 20 → buy; exit when a candle closes near the top of its range (IBS > 0.7) or above the previous high. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite in a downtrend.
m_bb: Below the Bollinger band, in the trend
Higher-timeframe uptrend; close below the lower Bollinger band (20, 2) → buy; exit back at the 20 average. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite above the upper band in a downtrend.
m_down3: Higher-timeframe uptrend; 3 lower closes in a row → buy; exit at the first higher close. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite (3 up) in a downtrend.
m_vwap: Stretch from VWAP in the trend
Higher-timeframe uptrend; price drops more than 1.5 ATR below the session VWAP → buy; exit back at VWAP. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite above VWAP in a downtrend.
m_rsi2x: More selective variant of x_rsi2: higher-timeframe uptrend, RSI 2 below 10 AND close near the bottom of the candle (IBS < 0.3) → buy; exit at RSI 2 > 60. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite in a downtrend.
m_wr: Williams %R at the floor, in the trend

Larry Williams: higher-timeframe uptrend and Williams %R (10) below −95 (close at the very bottom of the last 10 candles) → buy; exit when it climbs above −30. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite above −5 in a downtrend.
m_keltner: Below the Keltner channel, in the trend
Higher-timeframe uptrend; close below the bottom of the Keltner channel (EMA 20 − 2 ATR) → buy; exit back at the EMA 20. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite above the channel in a downtrend.
m_cci: Very low CCI, in the trend
Higher-timeframe uptrend; CCI (20) below −150 (price far below its usual average) → buy; exit when the CCI gets back above 0. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite above +150 in a downtrend.
m_stoch: Fast stochastic turning up, in the trend
Higher-timeframe uptrend; the fast stochastic (14, 3) was below 10 and turns up → buy; exit above 70. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite in a downtrend.
m_2ll: Two lower lows, in the trend

Connors: higher-timeframe uptrend; two candles in a row make a lower low AND close below the EMA 20 → buy; exit at the first close above the previous high. 1.5 ATR stop. Opposite (two higher highs) in a downtrend.
n_overnight: Well-documented effect (Cooper, Cliff & Gulen 2008; Kelly & Clark 2011): most of the US stock gains happen overnight. Buy at the 16:00 New York close (last candle of the session), sell on the first candle after the next day's open (09:35). Every night, no filter. 3% protective stop.
n_gapfill: If the Nasdaq opens 0.4% to 1.5% below the previous close (or above), it tends to come back to that close during the day. Entry at the close of the first 5-min candle in the gap-fill direction, target the previous close, stop at the same distance on the other side, exit at 15:55 at the latest.
n_firsthour: If the Nasdaq gained more than 0.5% between the open and 10:30 New York (or lost more than 0.5%), follow that direction until 15:55. Stop at half of the first hour's move (at least 1 ATR).
n_preholiday: Known calendar effect (Ariel 1990): US indices rise more often on the day before a New York Stock Exchange holiday. Buy at the close two days before the holiday, sell at the close of the day before. 2 ATR stop.
n_opex: Documented effect (Stivers & Sun 2013): US indices rise more often during monthly options expiration week (the week of the 3rd Friday). Buy at the previous Friday's close, sell at the 3rd Friday's close. 3 ATR stop.
n_santa: Known calendar effect (Santa Claus rally, Hirsch): the last 5 sessions of December and the first 2 of January are often positive. Buy at the close of the 6th trading day before year end, sell at the close of the 2nd trading day of January. 3 ATR stop.
n_weekrev: Nasdaq: rebound after a bad week

Weekly mean reversion in the trend: if the Nasdaq lost more than 3% over the week (5 sessions) while staying above its 200-day average, buy at the close; sell when it regains its 5-session high, or after 10 sessions. 3 ATR stop.
n_halfhalf: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018): the first half-hour return (09:30 → 10:00 New York) predicts the direction of the last half hour. Entry at 15:30 in the direction of the first half hour (if it moved more than 0.2%), exit at 15:55. 1.5 ATR stop.
n_trendday: At noon New York, if price is above the session VWAP AND above the open (buyers' day), buy until 15:55; opposite if below both. Stop below VWAP (at least 1 ATR).
n_drop: Nasdaq: rebound after a big one-day drop

Mean reversion: the Nasdaq loses more than 2.5% in one session while staying above its 200-day average → buy at the close; sell at the first close above the previous day's high, or after 5 sessions. 3 ATR stop.
n_reversal: The Nasdaq opens down more than 0.7% (gap) but closes above its open, in an uptrend (price > 200-day average): the morning sellers were absorbed. Buy at the close, sell at the next close above the day's high, or after 5 sessions. Stop below the day's low.
n_low10: Above the 200-day average, a close at the lowest of the last 10 sessions → buy; sell at a close at the highest of the last 5 sessions. 3 ATR stop.
n_yieldfall: When the US 10-year yield falls more than 5% in 5 sessions (e.g. 4.40% → 4.15%), growth stocks benefit: buy the Nasdaq if it is above its 50-day average, sell after 10 sessions or if rates get back above their 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
n_vixfade: The VIX (fear) jumps more than 30% in 3 sessions while the Nasdaq stays above its 200-day average → buy; sell when the VIX falls back below its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
n_ath: Trend following: buy when the Nasdaq closes at a new 1-year high (market in great shape), sell if the drop from the high reaches 5% (trailing stop on close). 3 ATR protective stop.
n_soxlead: Chips (SOX index) often lead tech: if the SOX gained at least 3 points more than the Nasdaq over 10 sessions and the Nasdaq is above its 50-day average, buy; sell after about 10 sessions (when the SOX lead fades) or if the Nasdaq falls below its 50 average. 3 ATR stop.
n_dollarfall: When the dollar index (DXY) falls more than 2% in 10 sessions, big tech companies (foreign revenue) benefit: buy the Nasdaq if it is above its 50-day average, sell when the dollar gets back above its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
n_bigup: A gain of more than 3% in one session, above the 200-day average, shows buyers arriving in force: buy at the close, sell after 10 sessions (close below the 10-day average) or at the 3 ATR stop.
n_mompb: Nasdaq: one-month pullback in a strong trend
The Nasdaq gained more than 10% in 3 months but fell over the last month: buy this pullback; sell when it regains its 20-session high, or if the 3-month gain disappears. 3 ATR stop.
n_rsi30: Nasdaq: RSI 14 below 30 in the trend
The most classic oversold signal: RSI 14 below 30 while the Nasdaq stays above its 200-day average → buy; sell when RSI 14 gets back above 50. 3 ATR stop.
n_2down: Nasdaq: two big drops in a row
Two sessions in a row down more than 1% each, above the 200-day average → buy at the close; sell at the first close above the previous day's high. 3 ATR stop.
n_oilfall: Oil falling more than 10% in 10 sessions lowers expected inflation and company costs: buy the Nasdaq if it is above its 50-day average; sell when oil gets back above its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
n_goldfall: When gold (safe haven) loses more than 4% in 10 sessions, investors take on risk again: buy the Nasdaq if it is above its 50-day average; sell when gold gets back above its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
n_rsspx: Tech leadership: invested when the Nasdaq 100 beats the S&P 500 over 3 months AND is above its 50-day average; out otherwise. 4 ATR stop.
n_rsi4: Nasdaq: RSI 4 below 20 in the trend
Best variant of the bulk test (346 strategies, npm run nas-grid): above the 200-day average, RSI 4 below 20 → buy; sell when RSI 4 gets back above 50. 3 ATR stop.
g_low10: Above its 200-day average, gold closes at the lowest of the last 10 sessions → buy; sell at a close at the highest of the last 5 sessions. 3 ATR stop.
g_weekrev: Gold: rebound after a bad week
Gold lost more than 3% in 5 sessions while staying above its 200-day average → buy; sell at the highest of the last 5 sessions. 3 ATR stop.
g_yieldfall: Gold pays no interest: when the US 10-year yield falls more than 5% in 5 sessions and gold is above its 50-day average → buy; sell when rates get back above their 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
g_dollarfall: Gold is priced in dollars: when the dollar index (DXY) falls more than 2% in 10 sessions and gold is above its 50-day average → buy; sell when the dollar gets back above its 10-day average. 3 ATR stop.
g_silverlead: When silver beats gold by at least 5 points over 10 sessions (the gold / silver ratio drops), metals are on the move: buy gold if it is above its 50-day average; sell when silver's lead fades or below the 50 average. 3 ATR stop.
g_oilfall: Best "other markets" rule of the gold bulk test: when oil loses more than 4% in 20 sessions and gold is above its 50-day average → buy; sell 20 sessions after the last signal. 3 ATR stop.
g_ibsh: Gold: candle closed low, exit above the high

Best total of the gold scalp bulk test (112 variants): in the 1 h trend, a 5-min candle closing in the bottom 20% of its range (IBS < 0.2) below the EMA 20 → buy; exit as soon as a close goes above the previous candle's high (mirror for shorts). 1.5 ATR stop, everything closed outside the session.
g_asia: Gold: mean reversion in the Asian session

Between 00:00 and 06:00 UTC (Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney; London and New York closed), the gold market is calm and often reverts to its average: in the 1 h trend, RSI 2 below 5 → buy (above 95 → sell in a downtrend), exit when RSI 2 crosses back over 60 (40), everything closed at 06:55. 1.5 ATR stop.
n_mom10: Nasdaq: the morning sets the end-of-day direction

Intraday momentum: if by 10:00 New York the Nasdaq has already moved more than 0.5% from the previous close (either way), take that direction at 15:00 and exit at 15:55. 3 ATR stop. Bulk test: +0.3% · +0.9% · +2.9% over 3 slices of 8 months, ≈ 0.5 trade per day.
n_orb15: If the session opened above the previous close, buy on the first 5-min close above the high of the first 15 minutes (before noon), stop at the low of that range, exit at 15:55. Bulk test: +3.5% · +0.6% · +2.0%, ≈ 0.4 trade per day.
n_orb5s: Sell on the first 5-min close below the low of the session's first 5 minutes (before noon), stop at the high of that range, exit at 15:55. Downside breakouts go further than upside ones intraday. Bulk test: +0.6% · +8.5% · +1.3%, ≈ 0.7 trade per day.
g_night: Literature (Blose, Gondhalekar & Kort 2014 / 2018; CBS thesis): gold gains mostly overnight and during Asian hours, and loses during the day. Buy at 21:00 UTC (New York close) Monday to Thursday, sell at 07:00 UTC (London open). 0.8% stop.
n_noise: Nasdaq: exit from the noise zone

Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (2024): the noise zone is the average move from the open, at each hour, over 14 days. On the half hours, buy if the Nasdaq breaks above it, sell below; exit when price crosses back over the VWAP or the boundary, everything closed at 15:55.
n_orbdir: Nasdaq: direction of the first 5-min candle
Zarattini & Aziz (2023): buy if the session's first 5-min candle is bullish, sell if it is bearish; stop at the other end of the candle, target 10× the risk, otherwise exit at 15:55.
g_orb30: Range from 07:00 to 07:30 UTC (London open). First 5-min close above the high → buy, below the low → sell (before 09:30 UTC); stop on the other side of the range, exit at 19:55 UTC. Spot gold 2009–2026: +24% · +22% · +24% over 3 slices, ≈ 1.25 trades per day.
